title: Watching Watergate hearings at the Gold Key Motel as F. Lee Bailey makes a pay-phone call

tellings.quote: I was sitting in the goldkey motel mhm with my investigator the William Johnstone Taylor

plain: In 1973 a lawyer named Dan Sheehan says he sat in the Gold Key Motel in Washington with his investigator, William Johnstone Taylor, watching the Senate hearings into the Watergate scandal, the break-in affair that shook the Nixon White House, while the famous defense lawyer F. Lee Bailey made a call from a pay phone. Sheehan tells it as something he was there for, and he names others around the scene, including the lawyer Gerald Alch, a man named Andy Toney, and the senators Daniel Inouye and Sam Ervin. He tells it as a small first-hand piece of how the people behind the scenes of the scandal were moving.
